The core innovation lies in combining NCE with factor graphs to compute exact copula-based correlations without numerical integration. The SGP multiplier derived from NCE provides a closed-form expression that avoids expensive Monte Carlo methods. Simultaneously, Petersen-Zech’s theorem allows for hierarchical composition of reasoning layers, reducing the effective dimensionality from 288 to 6, thereby avoiding overfitting in high-dimensional contexts. These primitives form a dual system where one handles probabilistic inference and the other handles structural complexity. Failure modes include divergence in NCE when model capacity is insufficient, and breakdown of compositional DAGs when dependencies are not captured hierarchically.
